customManagers.description: k3s release pins (INFRA-179): both Plans and the Ansible bootstrap version move together.

packageRules.description: Terraform providers and the CLI (INFRA-226): every PR plan runs with that workspace's write credentials, so a malicious release would run on the next Renovate cycle. Wait 7 days after a release before proposing it.
Same gate for the Terraform CLI pin in ci.yml (setup-terraform `terraform_version`, depName `terraform` in the github-actions manager), so the group never moves CI ahead of required_version.

Terraform CLI majors and minors (required_version in every stack and the ci.yml pin, one group) wait for a tick on the Dependency Dashboard, like k3s minors: an upgrade is planned, not proposed by a release (#260 and #315 closed, 2026-11-01). Patches still come, after the 7 days above.

Workspace cloudflare-tokens plans every PR with the bootstrap token, which can mint any Cloudflare token (INFRA-133): no provider bump branch, and so no plan, until the owner ticks it on the dashboard.
Database majors are one-way data-dir upgrades: never proposed. Upgrade by hand after a fresh dump (clusters/hetzner/data/RESTORE.md).

App images (contract section 8): production references are `:vX.Y.Z@sha256:<digest>`. Track release tags, ignore sha- tags, pin the digest (CI verifies its attestation). Merging the bump PR is still the deploy.
Digests are pinned only as part of a version bump: existing refs predate attestations and would fail the provenance check (INFRA-107), so they get pinned with their next release.

Staging follows releases (INFRA-36): bumps of manifests under a ziftbook-staging/ directory, majors included, merge without a PR once CI passes on the branch. Own branch prefix so a staging bump never shares a branch (and its automerge) with a production bump, which stays a PR. One group, so backend, frontend and migrations move together (a Renovate run while promote is retagging can still propose a partial set; the next run completes it).

Ziftbook production (INFRA-82): backend, worker, migrations and frontend move together in one PR, so a merge never runs a schema/code skew. No automerge: the PR is the deploy gate. Own branch prefix so it never shares a branch (and its automerge) with the staging bump.

TBD staging follows releases (INFRA-91), same as ziftbook-staging above: one grouped branch of backend, migrations, frontend and mcp, automerged by branch, own prefix so it never shares a branch with the tbd-prod PR.
TBD production (INFRA-43): backend, scheduler, migrations and frontend move together in one PR, so a merge never runs a schema/code skew. No automerge: the PR is the deploy gate.

Ziftbook v0.26.0 backend crashes at start (ModuleNotFoundError: mypy_boto3_s3, release smoke run 39116096441): never propose it. v0.26.1 is the fix; drop this rule once both environments run a later release.

k3s (INFRA-179): one grouped PR per release moves the Plans' version, k3s_version and the Plans' rancher/k3s-upgrade tag and digest together. separateMinorPatch, because v1.37.1 exists: without it Renovate offers only the minor and a v1.36.x patch never gets a branch. Minors need a dashboard tick (bump the k3s-ansible pin and the kubectl image patch in system-upgrade/kustomization.yaml with them).

The Plans pin rancher/k3s-upgrade as :<k3s version with - for +>@sha256:<index digest> (K8S-02); the kubernetes manager reads those lines and moves tag and digest in the k3s group above. Same scheme as k3s, so both resolve to the same release; rc and per-arch tags never match.
The k3s-upgrade digest moves only with a version: a digest-only update (the same tag pushed again) is never proposed.

k3s-ansible is pinned to the commit of tag 1.2.2 on purpose (ansible/requirements.yml); Renovate cannot look a commit up as a tag and warns on every run. Bump it by hand with the k3s upgrade (INFRA-179).

Third-party images (GHA-09): a release, or a new digest for a re-pushed tag, is proposed 7 days after it was published, as for k3s, so a broken or withdrawn release is caught first. Org images are not delayed: staging follows releases at once (INFRA-36, INFRA-91). Version and digest updates only: Renovate cannot age pins or replacements (it would hold them for ever), and a digest pin only freezes what already runs.
Same wait for third-party GitHub Actions and reusable workflows (GHA-09); the org's own are not delayed. Runner labels and setup-* version inputs are not matched here.

Only Docker Hub gives Renovate release timestamps; without one Renovate holds the update for ever (minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour defaults to timestamp-required). mirror.gcr.io (cloudflared, INFRA-152) has none, so its updates go ahead unaged, with a warning on the Dependency Dashboard.

Ansible CI tools (GHA-09): ansible/requirements-ci.txt pins ansible-core, ansible-lint and every dependency by hash, and Renovate rewrites the hashes with each bump. One grouped PR, so pins that depend on each other move together and the Ansible workflow installs them as a set, after the same 7-day wait. Renovate does not add a new dependency: when the install step says one is missing, regenerate the file with the command in its header.
